themes.label: Profanity/taboo and abusive slurs used for political delegitimization
defining_features: profanity_or_taboo_language (dehumanizing profanity terms like 'pigs', etc. when captured under taboo/insult)
themes.interpretation: When posts rely on explicit profanity or taboo slurs to insult political actors or groups, they are substantially more likely to be labeled remove—suggesting moderation targets abusive/harassing language.

themes.label: Ridicule/mocking epithets instead of substantive argument
defining_features: ridicule_or_mockery (dehumanizing animal/monster-style labels captured as mockery)
themes.interpretation: Mockery/epithets that dismiss groups rather than discuss policy tend to correlate with remove outcomes; moderation likely treats ridicule-focused content as harassment or low-credibility hostility.

themes.label: Normative moral condemnation plus explicit calls to ban/stop/remove
defining_features: call_to_action (direct instruction to remove/stop/act against a target)
themes.interpretation: Many posts that include moralized condemnation combined with direct policy prescriptions appear in both groups, but the theme captures a consistent “instructional activism” pattern that may be acceptable when not paired with severe abuse/profanity.

themes.label: Us-vs-them directional blame and outgroup characterizations
defining_features: mirror_shift_direction (retargeting blame from one cause to another, still directional)
themes.interpretation: Directional blame toward political blocs (often framed as deceitful, dangerous, fascist, etc.) appears across both labels, but it becomes more risky when paired with harassment, extreme labels, or violent/expansive in-group-out-group prescriptions.

themes.label: Conspiratorial/disinformation framing as explanation
defining_features: conspiratorial_framing (lists of conspiracy streams like QAnon/Flat Earth)
themes.interpretation: Posts that explain politics via disinfo plots, propaganda/gaslighting, or named conspiracy movements are more likely to be removed in this corpus, indicating moderation concern with conspiracy-style claims.

themes.label: High-contrast emphasis and emphatic formatting (all-caps, ellipses, punctuation intensity)
defining_features: high_punctuation_intensity (multiple punctuation marks, ellipses, dense expressive punctuation)
high_contrast_label_pair (slash-separated ideological labeling) when used for emphatic categorization
themes.interpretation: Strong emphasis/formatting is common in kept posts here and is less consistently associated with remove on its own—suggesting intensity alone isn’t the primary moderation trigger unless paired with abusive/profane content.

themes.label: Policy domain focus: guns/weapons regulation and gun violence
defining_features: primary_policy_domain (gun violence / gun rights / assault-weapon ban / open carry)
themes.interpretation: Gun-policy discussions cluster as a major topic, and in this shard most are kept—moderation appears more sensitive to abusive language/conspiracies than to the policy domain itself.

themes.label: Policy domain focus: abortion/reproductive rights (including moral rights framing)
defining_features: primary_policy_domain (abortion pill / abortion access / abortion debate)
themes.interpretation: Reproductive-rights content appears in both labels; risk likely increases when abortion is expressed via highly inflammatory taboo framing or extreme abusive insults captured elsewhere.

themes.label: Calls for targeted action against systems/agents (implicating institutions like ICE, governments, or specific agencies)
defining_features: call_to_action (direct instruction to governments/agencies or to enforce/act)
second_person_direct_address (imperatives directed to an entity, e.g., 'ICE can start...')
themes.interpretation: Some posts advocate concrete operational changes (e.g., agency enforcement behavior, eligibility oversight). In this corpus they appear more often in keep than remove, implying that action-oriented content is acceptable when not expressed as abusive harassment.

themes.label: Victimhood/persecution framing and harm-to-innocents rhetoric
defining_features: victimhood_or_persecution_framing (mass shooting tragedy used as political exploitation evidence)
themes.interpretation: Where posts frame events as exploitation of tragedy or persecution of protected groups, they more often fall under keep in this dataset—suggesting that harm/victim narratives are not, by themselves, a remove trigger.

cross_cutting_themes: Profanity/taboo abuse and ridicule/mocking frequently co-occur with outgroup blame (Themes 1, 2, 4), which correlates with higher remove rates.
Emphatic formatting/intensity (Theme 6) spans both labels and appears to be a lower-risk feature unless paired with abusive language (Themes 1–2).
Conspiratorial/disinformation explanation (Theme 5) can combine with directional blame (Theme 4), increasing the likelihood of remove in this corpus.
Policy-domain topics (Themes 7–8) are moderated more by the rhetorical style (Themes 1–6) than by the underlying issue category.
